Perfect — thanks Jordan. A few specifics from our side to make the evals as useful as possible:

Recommended model variants to run (quick guidance):
- redwood-10b-optim (default baseline): best quality for long-context summarization, expect ~120ms token latency on Dedicated pools.
- redwood-4b-quant (cost-optimized): good for high-throughput triage where short summaries suffice.
- If you have very long threads (>2k tokens) include a few examples; we can test kv-cache scaling.

What to include in the prompt CSV (use attached prompt_set_template.csv):
- id, scenario, prompt_text, expected_output_hint, sensitivity_flags (PHI/PII/PCI), language, notes on edge cases
- Please label a couple of "must-pass" prompts (these are hard correctness checks).

Benchmarks / tooling we will share:
- Eval dashboard (we'll populate after our run): https://app.redwood.com/eval-dashboard/ACME-4512
- Initial run: we typically produce an eval report and a short PDF summary (attached as eval_results_summary.pdf once ready).

Redaction notes (short): if you can replace exact identifiers with consistent tokens (e.g., <ACCOUNT_NUM_1>) that preserves formatting for the model while avoiding sending raw PHI. See attached redaction_guidance.pdf for examples.

Once we receive the prompts, Aditya will run the model-fit eval (48-72 hours turnaround) and we'll send a summary + recommended configuration. After that we schedule a 30-min sync to review results and agree on rollouts.

If you want, propose 2 slots next week and I can book Aditya.

Thanks — looking forward.

Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attached is our first pass: acme_prompts_v1.csv. Highlights / notes:

- Edge cases called out in the CSV: mixed-language threads (EN/ES), extremely long customer threads (>3000 tokens after concatenation), inline code blocks from engineering, shorthand/slang in transcripts.
